מִבְּלִי אִישׁ עֹבֵר divided as rule 48 divides a privative מִן — 'so that' to the preposition — with 'none' fusing בְּלִי and אִישׁ under rule 30 and headed on the negation; the alternative marks אִישׁ unrepresented and is named at the unit. The negation stays with בְּלִי rather than with מִן because a negation morpheme is actually present here, unlike rule 48's bare privative.

The מִן…עַד figure is rendered 'both … and': 'both' goes to מִן and 'and' to the waw, leaving עַד unrepresented. Rule 14's correlative clause would give the pair to the waw alone, but it governs only where nothing else licenses the opening word.

'men' is a lexical English subject noun supplied where no source nominal stands, and is added under rule 17; the article of הַשָּׁמַיִם takes the 'the' standing before its own word, the construct taking a supplied one (rule 29).
